m.kripalu.cha1: O mind, worship the gracious Śrī Rāmacandra, who takes away the dreadful fear of worldly existence. His eyes are like fresh lotuses; his face, his hands and his red feet are lotuses too.
m.kripalu.cha2: His boundless beauty outshines countless Kāmadevas; he is lovely as a fresh dark rain cloud. His yellow garment gleams like pure lightning. I bow to him, the husband of Janaka's daughter.
m.kripalu.cha3: Worship him, the friend of the lowly, radiant as the sun, destroyer of the lines of the demons; the joy of Raghu's house, the root of bliss, the moon of Kośala, the son of Daśaratha.
m.kripalu.cha4: A crown on his head, earrings, a tilaka on his brow; his fair, noble limbs adorned with ornaments. His arms reach to his knees; he bears bow and arrows, and conquered Khara and Dūṣaṇa in battle.
m.kripalu.cha5: Thus says Tulasīdāsa: O delight of the minds of Śaṅkara, Śeṣa and the sages, destroyer of the host of the wicked, lust and the rest, make your home in the lotus of my heart.
